issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to provide an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]), but the solution implements init(books: Set<Book>) in Bookstore. This mismatch prevents students from following the specified constructor signature and will cause confusion (and a type error) when assigning or creating a Bookstore using an array of Book.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer accept an array of Book to match the problem statement: change the signature in Bookstore to init(books: [Book]) (and ensure template and solution use the same signature). Alternatively, if a Set is intended, update the problem statement to require init(books: Set<Book>), but the recommended fix is to use [Book] as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (an array), but the solution implements init(books: Set<Book>) (a set). This mismatch of the initializer parameter type for the same conceptual API (the Bookstore constructor) creates a mapping confusion: students expect to pass an array of Book as specified in the problem and as used when assembling the bookstore, but the solution's initializer uses a different collection type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature consistent with the problem statement and client usage: change the solution to use init(books: [Book]) and assign self.books = books. In other words, replace init(books: Set<Book>) with init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books } so the constructor accepts an array as specified.
